text:
Situation: Lidocaine hydrochloride injection has been on the FDA drug shortage list since 2012-02-22 and remains current as of 2026-10-21. Corvale Lakeside holds 3.9–4.2 days of supply across six presentations. Corvale General holds approximately 6 days across six presentations. Corvale East holds 10.4–36.5 days across six presentations.

Why (FDA record): FDA inspection 639034 at Hospira, Inc. ended 2010-01-19 and was classified OAI, 764 days before the shortage posting. A Warning Letter was issued to Hospira, Inc. on 2010-04-12, 681 days before the shortage posting. FDA inspection 732886 at Hospira, Inc. ended 2011-06-17 and was classified OAI, 250 days before the shortage posting. FDA inspection 740633 at Hospira, Inc. ended 2011-08-04 and was classified OAI, 202 days before the shortage posting. FDA inspection 732653 at Fresenius Kabi USA, LLC ended 2011-07-08 and was classified OAI, 229 days before the shortage posting.

Our position: Internal transfers can stabilize Lakeside and General within days. Alternate manufacturer product is approved and available. External purchases from suppliers not on the FDA shortage list are viable.

Recommended actions:
1. Transfer 204 units of lidocaine hydrochloride 20 mg/mL 50 mL MDV from Corvale East to Corvale Lakeside. Approval: Pharmacy Director.
2. Transfer 227 units of lidocaine hydrochloride anhydrous and dextrose monohydrate from Corvale East to Corvale General. Approval: Pharmacy Director.
3. Procure lidocaine hydrochloride 20 mg/mL from Medical Purchasing Solutions, LLC using the approved substitute NDC. Approval: Pharmacist.
4. Evaluate purchase from Avenacy, LLC (ADAPTIS plant) and A-S Medication Solutions for additional supply. Approval: Buyer.

Not recommended: Delay transfers pending new vendor qualification; the approved alternate manufacturer and internal stock can cover immediate needs.
